summary: Iteration 3 regression for Bodhi.ai new features (multi-textbook, async generation, custom_instructions, format_distribution, PDF blocking, brand mark). 9 of 10 backend tests passed (1 skipped because no failed papers exist to verify 409-on-failed in DB; logic was code-reviewed and is correct). Frontend smoke for /papers/new fully green: brand mark, format mix card, sliders, custom instructions textarea, and custom format chip all work.

frontend_smoke_passed.brand_mark: Header .brand-mark shows 'Bodhi.ai' with .ai accent (no 'BodhLai' kerning bug)

critical_code_review_comments: MINOR: NewPaper.jsx renders <span> with x-component instrumentation inside <option>, causing a React hydration warning in console. Functionality unaffected; likely from Emergent's source-tracking babel plugin. Worth investigating only if hydration warnings need to be eliminated.

INFO: server.py /api/papers/generate uses asyncio.create_task without referencing the task. If the event loop is cancelled the task may be GC'd; in current production this is fine but storing task refs would be safer.
test_credentials: pdftest@t.com / pass123 (existing seeded teacher). Second teacher registered dynamically per run (second_teacher_<ts>@t.com / pass1234).
seed_data_creation: Each run uploads 2 fresh dummy textbooks (Physics + Chemistry, class 10) for the seeded teacher. Several pending/ready papers are created and left in DB.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend regression file at /app/backend/tests/test_new_features.py exercises all 6 new feature areas. Note: external proxy is occasionally slow (>30s read), so http timeouts are set to 60-90s. Set REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL env var explicitly when running pytest from CLI: `REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=https://question-ai-10.preview.emergentagent.com python -m pytest tests/test_new_features.py -v`. The test_pdf_blocked_on_failed test will skip if no failed papers exist; that is expected behaviour. Universal LLM key worked throughout this run.
rca_of_the_issue: First pytest run had 4 failures all due to `requests.ReadTimeout` from the public preview proxy (read timeout=15-30s) — not a backend bug. Backend logs showed all underlying calls returned 200. Increased HTTP timeouts to 60-90s; all tests then passed.
